# #643 — flaky: ob-backfill quadratic-blowup test asserts an absolute wall-clock threshold (1005ms vs 1000ms)

State: OPEN
Author: rodaddy
Labels: none
Created: 2026-08-08T16:53:54Z
Updated: 2026-08-08T16:53:54Z

---

`scripts/ob-backfill.test.ts:259` asserts a wall-clock duration:

```ts
expect(performance.now() - startedAt).toBeLessThan(1_000);
```

Observed failing in CI at **1005.5852320000013 ms** — missing by 5.6 ms — on run 31267844990 (`db-integration`, `Test (JUnit reporter for the anti-skip guard)`). A re-run of the **same SHA** (30efb2a, run 31267860992) passed with the identical tree, so this is timing, not behavior. Suite result on the failing run: 3711 pass / 34 skip / **1 fail**.

This is the flake class already recorded in `docs/lane-contract.md` Tightenings (2026-08-08 round 5): "Wall-clock assertions (`toBeLessThan(1000)` ms) are CI flake generators" — previously filed as #632 and #634 for other instances. A shared runner under load makes any absolute millisecond threshold a coin flip near the boundary.

**What the test is actually defending:** that `sanitize()` is not quadratic in token count. That property is better expressed as a RATIO between two input sizes (e.g. 12k tokens takes < ~4x the time of 3k tokens) than as an absolute ceiling, because the ratio is robust to a slow or contended runner while still failing loudly on real quadratic blowup.

Found by the #563 lane (PR #639), which does not touch this file — reported rather than absorbed, per the lane contract.
